title: Exam preparation by topic
description: Tie the available time to topics, log the sessions and check separately what has already been learned.

blocks.text: A student spreads the topics out up to the exam date and notes what they worked on. A short summary can be added to a session: what has been worked through and what is still giving trouble. The next session is chosen from that picture, not just from a run of launches.

quote.text: Flora has completely transformed how I study for the LSAT. Keeps me organize, motivated, and way more productive!

blocks.text: To begin with, one exam, a list of topics and a revision of the plan after a missed day are enough. Checking knowledge has to be a separate action; a long timer must not be turned automatically into a “learned” mark.
A timer does not test knowledge

General praise for LSAT preparation confirms the value of being organized for one author. It does not prove that a new planner will improve an exam result. It is worth finding out whether tying a topic to a session helps in choosing the next useful step.
